course.title: Retrieval and Knowledge Engineering for Language Model Systems
course.tagline: Build and measure the retrieval layer of a language model system: search, corpus preparation, access, agents and structured data
course.description: Participants build and measure the retrieval layer of a language model system for a fictional university: bilingual regulations, study plans with tables, scanned Arabic circulars and an enrolment statistics warehouse. Starting from a graded test set, they build lexical, dense, hybrid and reranked search with Arabic normalisation, parse and chunk documents by structure, filter by date and role, give an agent search tools and a small knowledge graph, and answer statistical questions through a semantic layer instead of free text-to-SQL.
course.audience: Practitioners. Engineers who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: a deployed model or language model application they built and can explain.
prerequisites: AE-202 Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals
AE-203 Building Applications on Language Models
Has built a small grounded application with citations
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Prepare a retrieval test set with graded relevance judgements and compute standard ranking metrics for each language, given 60 Arabic and English queries over the corpus
outcomes.evidence: a versioned test set and a report of recall at 10, reciprocal rank and discounted cumulative gain by language

outcomes.text: Implement lexical, dense, hybrid and reranked search with Arabic normalisation and compare them on quality and latency, given the corpus and the test set
outcomes.evidence: a results table with ranking metrics and 95th-percentile latency per method

outcomes.text: Analyse parsing and chunking choices by scoring two parsers and two chunking schemes, given 30 scanned and digital pages with tables
outcomes.evidence: a parsing score per page type and a retrieval comparison with a recommendation

outcomes.text: Build retrieval that never returns a document the requester may not see or a superseded rule, given role labels and effective dates on every chunk
outcomes.evidence: a passing suite of leak and staleness tests

outcomes.text: Design an agentic search component that chooses among search tools and a small knowledge graph within a context budget, given 15 multi-step questions, a graph of linked course rules and a token budget
outcomes.evidence: traces and a comparison with single-shot search on accuracy, tool calls and tokens

outcomes.text: Evaluate free text-to-SQL against a semantic layer with validated SQL and decide which to ship, given 20 statistical questions with reference answers
outcomes.evidence: execution accuracy for both and a one-page decision memo

case_study.name: Al-Nuha University
case_study.summary: Al-Nuha University is a fictional public university with six colleges whose regulations assistant, Nibras, answers students and staff from bilingual regulations, study plans with tables, scanned Arabic circulars, staff-only records and an enrolment statistics warehouse. Participants build and measure Nibras's retrieval layer on about 3,000 synthetic pages and a synthetic warehouse, generated with a fixed seed, with planted problems: dialect queries, broken parses, superseded rules, near-duplicate circulars, mislabelled staff pages and warehouse traps.

capstone.summary: A measured retrieval layer for the university's assistant, or for a synthetic or public corpus the participant brings, submitted as a public repository whose README reports metrics by language, leak and staleness tests, latency and cost per question, then an eight-minute defence and four minutes of questions
capstone.submission: A public repository whose README reports, for the participant's retrieval layer, the ranking metrics by language and query type on a versioned test set, the leak and staleness test results, the 95th-percentile latency by stage and the cost per question, with the code, the test set and the run files committed. Then an eight-minute defence that runs one query live and explains one failure by component, and four minutes of questions.
